## Fixed decisions
1. **What becomes a key.** Visible text, aria labels, titles, placeholders,
   empty states, toasts and errors are all catalogue keys, and "Apunta" is never
   translated. This holds for a string **wherever it is written**: a JSX text
   node, one of the four visible attributes, a module-level const, or the
   argument of a thrown `Error`. `RefineColumn.tsx:15`'s
   `SAVE_BEFORE_CHAT_ERROR` — a full user-visible sentence that reaches the
   screen from `:120` — is a key like any other, and it is a **UI** key, not
   `errors.<code>`: S2.2's Fixed decision 9 reserves that namespace for the
   server's codes and S2.5 owns the list.
2. **Keep-as-is tokens, and the two ways one can arrive.** A keep-as-is token
   that is a **whole literal** (`aria-label="Apunta"`, and nothing else in the
   owned set today) stays in `scripts/check-ui-strings.allow.json`, matched
   whole — and that file is **not** this card's to edit, so a token that needs
   adding is reported, not added. A keep-as-is token **inside** a translatable
   sentence is preserved verbatim in **both** catalogue values, never
   allowlisted, never dropped, never translated: `RefineColumn.tsx:15` (`Apunta`
   inside the save-failure sentence) is this card's known case and
   `Capture.tsx:389` (`Mac` inside `recorded. Nothing has left this Mac.`) is
   the same class in S2.4's file, named so the rule is not rediscovered. The
   allowlist matches whole strings only, so the in-sentence token can be
   neither allowlisted nor split off into a key of its own.
3. **The mount is this card's, and a green row does not prove it.**
   `web/src/App.tsx:38-42` is where `SettingsProvider` is mounted, no card in S2
   was licensed to touch it, and S2.2's Fixed decision 10 assigns the mount
   here because this is the first card whose components call `t()`. The change
   is the import and one wrapper element, above the router, and every owned
   component reads its strings through `useI18n()` under that provider. So a
   V2 at `TOTAL 0` with the provider still unmounted is a **stop**, not a pass:
   the first note view rendered outside it would throw. `web/src/lib/i18n.tsx`
   falls back to English when no provider is above it, which is exactly why the
   rows cannot see the difference on their own.
4. **A date reaches a catalogue as a parameter, never as English text.**
   `NoteView.tsx:578-580` composes `{patient} · created {…}` and
   ` · edited {…}` from `formatNoteDate` / `formatEditedDate`, and both helpers
   return English sentences from `web/src/lib/format.ts` — `'Today'` at `:34`,
   lowercase `'today'` at `:41`, otherwise the hardcoded `en-US`
   `Intl.DateTimeFormat` at `:20-24`. Each sentence becomes one key whose date
   parameter is declared `date` (an ISO timestamp, formatted in the local zone
   through the option set S2.2's Fixed decision 5 fixed, which is what the
   seeded `note.updatedAt` is pinned to), so `Aug 8, 2026` is produced by `t()`
   and never handed to it. **Passing the pre-formatted English as a `{day}`
   param is the failure this decision forbids**: V2 goes green, English is
   unchanged, and the note view keeps saying `Aug 8, 2026` in Spanish until
   S2.7's copy review finds it. The same-day cases are two named keys, not a
   `format.ts` edit: `notes.today` (already seeded, `Today` / `Hoy`, pinned to
   `format.ts:34`) for the created sentence, and a new `note.editedToday`
   whose English is `format.ts:41`'s lowercase `today` and whose es-MX follows
   S1.4 §2.4. The same-day test is a local-date comparison over the two ISO
   values the component already holds (`format.ts:26-28` is the shape), so no
   helper is added and **no line of `format.ts` or `plural.ts` changes** — they
   stay S2.2's oracle, and S2.2's Fixed decision 6 (English equals what the app
   produces today) carries over unchanged.
5. **The checker is necessary, not sufficient, and the two blind spots are
   pinned by tests.** A literal is "JSX text nodes plus the `placeholder`,
   `aria-label`, `title` and `alt` string attributes"
   (`check-ui-strings.mjs:29-36`), and the pieces JSX leaves when it splits a
   sentence around an interpolation or an inline element are deliberately not
   reported. So V2 at `TOTAL 0` is compatible with two classes of in-scope
   string still hardcoded, and both exist today: a string held in a module const
   (`RefineColumn.tsx:15`, the blind spot Fixed decision 1 covers) and a
   sentence split around an inline element (`HomeLauncher.tsx:137`'s
   `New: <strong>{query.trim()}</strong>`). Each is pinned where a row can see
   it: `web/src/components/RefineColumn.test.tsx` gains one case asserting the
   rendered save-failure text is `t('…')`'s English, and
   `web/src/components/HomeLauncher.test.tsx` gains one asserting the rendered
   `New:` line is the catalogue's English with the typed name in it. Both files
   exist and V1 collects them.
6. **One owner per shared component.** `Dialog.tsx`, `ConfirmDialog.tsx`,
   `Toast.tsx` and `icons.tsx` are this card's; S2.4 is told they are
   read-only. `BrainstormView` and `Workspace` use the first two and
   `Workspace` uses `Toast`, so without this sentence both cards would claim
   the same three files and the boundary would be whichever implementer
   arrived second. `ChatComposer.tsx`, `ThinkingDots.tsx`,
   `InterventionApproachSuggestion.tsx` and `NoteBody.tsx` are this card's for
   the same reason, and `SpellLayer.tsx` / `SpellMarks.tsx` — reached through
   `NoteBody` and `ChatComposer` — are S2.4's, which is why they are absent
   from the owned list and from V2's paths.
7. **The catalogue grows; the guard does not.** New keys go into both
   `en.ts` and `es-MX.ts` and nowhere else, and the type-level parity rule
   (S2.2's Fixed decision 2) is what stops a key that es-MX lacks — V4 is its
   only witness, since vitest strips types. `shared/src/i18n/t.test.ts` is in
   May edit for the one purpose its May edit entry names, and nothing else in
   it moves. A key this card cannot fill with a real es-MX string is reported,
   not filled with the English.

| V4 | `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/apunta-node/node-v24.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" && npm run lint && npm run typecheck` | exit 0. `lint` ends in the bare `node scripts/check-ui-strings.mjs`, which is still report-only, so it contributes output and never a non-zero exit — a red lint from that step means `REPORT_ONLY` was flipped, which is S2.4's switch and HS-7 (Must not edit). `typecheck` is where the **type-level** parity lives: `es-MX.ts`'s `satisfies Record<MessageKey, Message>` is a `tsc` error for a key this card added to `en` and forgot, and the `// @ts-expect-error` case in `shared/src/i18n/t.test.ts` — which this card may not touch — proves the same rule from the other side, so an unused `@ts-expect-error` is itself an error and the case cannot go vacuous. A `tsc` error in a file this card does not own is a stop, not something to fix here |
| V5 | `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/apunta-node/node-v24.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" && rm -rf /tmp/apunta-v2-s2.3-negative && mkdir -p /tmp/apunta-v2-s2.3-negative && cp web/src/components/HomeLauncher.tsx /tmp/apunta-v2-s2.3-negative/Probe.tsx && printf '\nexport function S23Probe(): React.JSX.Element {\n  return <p>Not translated yet</p>;\n}\n' >> /tmp/apunta-v2-s2.3-negative/Probe.tsx && node scripts/check-ui-strings.mjs --report /tmp/apunta-v2-s2.3-negative/Probe.tsx` | exit **0** (report-only) and the report is **exactly one line** plus `TOTAL 1`: the planted `Not translated yet`, named with the copied file's own path. The four literals this card removes from `HomeLauncher.tsx` are **absent** from it, so `TOTAL 1` is the criterion rather than `TOTAL 5` (which is what the base-commit file reports) — the row is the negative case V2 cannot be, and it is what makes "no literals left" mean something: a checker that scans nothing, that ignores a path argument outside `web/src`, or that reports the whole tree prints more than one line and fails this row while passing V2. Nothing is written inside the checkout and the temp folder is disposable |

All five rows run on this box as written, and every one of them exports the
provisioned Node first: the root `engines` is `>=24.19.0 <25`
(`package.json:8-10`) and `.nvmrc` is `24.19.0`, while the box default is
**v26.8.2** — outside it, and V1 goes red for a reason no card owns, because
Node 26's experimental `localStorage` global shadows jsdom's and fails 3 of the
6 cases in `web/src/lib/appearance.test.ts`
(`docs/v2/state/reviews/P0.5-impl.md:122-134`). A row that runs outside
`engines` is a row whose result the card cannot defend. V1, V2, V4 and V5 launch
nothing — in-process vitest, a `node` script over the working tree, eslint,
prettier or `tsc` — so they run bare rather than through
`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs` (AM-025). Only V3 starts anything, and it goes
through `sandbox.mjs` on port 7822. The counts quoted in V1 and V2 were measured
at the base commit `4eaed50` on this box (Node v24.19.0, vitest 4.1.11, ICU
78.3) and are reproducible by running the same commands there.

`docs/v2/evidence/S2.3/` (AM-017) carries one file per row, `v1.md` … `v5.md`,
each with RUN-CONFIG §4's fields: working directory (repository root), the exact
command as the row writes it, exit code, start and end time, and the runner's
own output. V1 records the test names (`--reporter=verbose`) and the collected
file count, V2 its `TOTAL` line and the number it fell from, V3 the collected
test count and the `runId` the `env` step printed (raw logs stay in the run
folder), V4 both tools' tails, V5 the report verbatim. Sanitise as RUN-CONFIG
§4 says (`<sandbox>`, `~`, no hostnames or real names); the sample name is the
prototype's `John Smith` (HS-8).

## Stop conditions
- A string is built by concatenation that cannot be expressed with one key and
  parameters: **report** it with its location, and do not split it into two keys
  to make it fit. `formatDayGap`'s two-direction `in 12 days` / `12 days ago`
  and `formatRelativeTime`'s `just now` / `yesterday` are the known shape, and
  they are the ones S2.3 pins keys to (S2.2's stop names them for this card).
- A literal in an owned file that can be neither keyed nor allowlisted —
  `RefineColumn.tsx:15` and `Capture.tsx:389` are the known cases — is
  **reported** with its `file:line`, and `scripts/check-ui-strings.allow.json`
  is **not** edited to absorb it (HS-9). The response is a `BLOCKED` return
  naming the line, not a widened May edit and not a new key invented to dodge
  the question.
- A `tsc` error in a file this card does not own, or any red assertion in one,
  is a `BLOCKED` return with the compiler output. Do not make a field optional
  to quiet the compiler, and do not relax an assertion (HS-7). Two routes lead
  here and both are known: retyping `TopBarProps` / `ScreenProps` to take a key
  instead of `back.label: string` types every route call site, all of them
  them S2.4's; and the nine-key pin in `shared/src/i18n/t.test.ts`, which is
  why that file is in May edit.
- The refine chat's error lines come from `web/src/hooks/useDictation.ts` and
  `web/src/lib/recorder.ts`, which **no S2 card owns** (`recorder.ts` is Must
  not edit): they stay English and are reported as a finding for a later card —
  do not widen May edit for them.
- The provider needs its mount, or a screen's string needs a file this card does
  not own: a `BLOCKED` return naming the file and the coordinator amendment it
  would take, not a quiet widening. `web/src/App.tsx` is licensed above for the
  mount only; mounting is S2.2's stop condition for itself and this card's for
  the real tree.
- The bare checker default would have to become failing for any row to go green:
  stop. That switch is S2.4's, and making it here to quiet a red row is HS-7.
- A key this card adds has no real es-MX text, or a date would have to reach a
  catalogue pre-formatted (Fixed decision 4): **report** it with its key and its
  location rather than shipping the English or the `Aug 8, 2026`. A copy
  question is not a card defect — S2.7 and S2.8 own the copy — but an English
  string in `es-MX.ts` is neither copy nor catalogue.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-LANG@1 Language, documents and jobs

**Built by** S2.1. **Proven by** S2.6, S4b.1, S5.6. **Consumers:** web,
server routes, AI prompts, guards, speech, spell check, formats, backup.

1. Setting `language` ∈ `en` | `es-MX`, default `en`. The server exposes
   `spanishAvailable: boolean`: true only when `APUNTA_DEV_SPANISH=1` (D12).
   When false, the Language control is hidden and `es-MX` is rejected by
   `PUT /api/settings` with code `language_unavailable`.
2. Locale mapping (one table in `shared/src/i18n/locales.ts`):

   | App | UI and `Intl` | Whisper `-l` | Speech model | Dictionary | Prompts |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `en` | unchanged from today | `en` | `ggml-tiny.en.bin` | current English | current |
   | `es-MX` | `es-MX` | `es` | per C-STT selection | per S1.5 | Spanish set |

3. Documents: migration adds `locale TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en'` to notes
   and to formats. **All existing rows are `en`.** New notes take the job's
   locale. Existing notes and formats are never translated or relabelled.
4. Jobs capture `{ locale, sttModel, llmModel, promptSet }` at start
   (recording, transcription, draft, refine, plan, briefing, brainstorm).
   Retries, SSE and persistence use the captured context, never the current
   setting. **Refine uses the target note's locale**, whatever the UI
   language and whatever language the request is typed in.
5. Section roles: `shared/src/section-roles.ts` maps known section names in
   both languages (case- and accent-insensitive) to role IDs (`location`,
   `presentation`, `risk`, `discussion`, `intervention`, `actions`,
   `next_session`, and the SOAP and intake roles). Guards use roles, not
   strings. Unknown sections get role `custom`. Stored strings are not
   rewritten.
6. Changing Language is blocked while any job or save is active: the web
   control is disabled with a reason; the server also returns 409
   `language_change_blocked` if it knows of an active job.
7. Spanish dictation requires the Spanish speech model to be ready (C-ACQ).
   If it is not, dictation shows "Spanish speech model not installed" with
   a download action. **Spanish audio is never sent to the English model.**
8. The Spanish standard format is created as a separate format with
   `locale: 'es-MX'`; English formats are untouched. Imported formats take
   the UI language at import time; the user can change a format's locale.
9. Backups and restores carry the `locale` columns.

**Rejection example.** UI switched to Español, user refines an existing
English note with a Spanish instruction → the note stays English, the reply
explains the change in the note's language.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.
